1973: An early frost on September 21 and a hard freeze the next night. Maine's 210 cwt an acre was the lowest yield of the period, and the price was high at $7.25 a hundredweight.
1974: A normal season with few hot days. Maine dug 260 cwt an acre from 140,000 acres, and the price fell to $2.90.
1975: Late blight was severe in southeastern Pennsylvania, and early August in upstate New York was very favorable to it. McCain bought a French-fry plant at Washburn.
1976: The earliest fall frost on record came on September 3. In May the New York Mercantile Exchange declared a default on its May Maine potato contract.
1977: One of the worst summers for blight weather in the record, by the Blitecast count of severity values.
1978: Frost came on September 14, one of the earliest of the period, and the yield fell to 220 cwt an acre.
1980: Caribou's earliest night at 24°F came on September 29, and some 4,000 planted acres were never harvested. The price was high at $7.25.
1981: Maine's mandatory certified-seed law took effect this season, raising the price of seed and, by one study's estimate, yields.
1984: Only about a tenth of the Maine crop was still picked by hand, and Presque Isle schools closed for three weeks so students could work the harvest.
1985: A cool summer with only four days at 85°F. Maine's 28.2 million hundredweight was the largest crop of the period, and the price fell to $2.80.
1986: After the big 1985 crop the price more than doubled, to $6.00. The Maine Potato Board was founded.
1988: One of the worst summers for blight weather in the record, by the Blitecast count of severity values.
1989: The first frost came on September 4. Maine gave up the 165-pound barrel as its measure for buying and selling potatoes and switched to the hundredweight.
1990: About 5,000 of the 81,000 planted acres went unharvested, the largest share of the period; the record does not say why.
1991: The driest July in the record, under an inch of rain at Caribou, then a wet August. The yield fell to 230 cwt an acre.
1992: A cool, wet summer with one hot day. Maine averaged 300 cwt an acre, and irrigation added only 4% in University of Maine trials.
1993: The US-8 strain of late blight turned up in Maine, the only state where it was found that year.
1994: Late blight was especially severe across the Northeast, with foliage destroyed and severe tuber blight. Maine's yield fell to 245 cwt an acre.
1995: The driest summer on record at Caribou, 5.6 inches. Maine's 220 cwt an acre was the worst year against trend, and irrigation added 37% in University of Maine trials.
2002: The latest spring frost on record came on June 4, and August brought only about half an inch of rain.
2004: A cool summer with one hot day and a big crop of 310 cwt an acre. With prices low, a quarter of the crop was lost, dumped or left unsold.
2006: Frost came on September 11, one of the earliest of the period. Late blight was found in fields across northern and central Aroostook.
2007: Good weather let growers keep their fungicide sprays to a minimum.
2008: The threat of blight called for heavier and more frequent sprays. A hard freeze came on September 19, the earliest of the period.
2009: A wet June and July, 22 of 30 days with rain or no sun, kept growers off their fields. Late blight came in on tomato transplants but largely spared commercial potatoes.
2010: No late blight was reported in Maine.
2011: The wettest summer in the record, with a record 7.9 inches of rain in July and Irene on August 28. Late blight was found around Bridgewater, Caribou and Fort Fairfield, but it was no epidemic.
2012: A warm July with under two inches of rain, and the yield fell below trend to 275 cwt an acre.
2013: The second-wettest May to September in the record at Caribou.
2015: The University of Maine released the Caribou Russet.
2016: Maine harvested 46,500 acres, the fewest of the period.
2018: Twenty-five days at 85°F or more and a dry summer, yet the yield of 310 cwt an acre was right on trend.
2019: A late spring, with the last frost on May 28.
2020: Drought: under five inches of rain from June 1 to late August, and Aroostook was declared a drought disaster area. A hard freeze came on September 21.
2021: Warm and moderately dry. Maine averaged 345 cwt an acre.
2022: Maine set its yield record, 355 cwt an acre.
2023: A very wet summer, with 6.6 inches of rain at Caribou in August. The harvest stalled in September and some low spots were left undug.
2024: Late blight was found on August 9 in a Presque Isle field, and growers everywhere were told to spray every five days. September was the second driest on record at Caribou.
